implementation.replacementStatus: partial; custom-effect completion, single-string and default-object animation built, full renderer pending
implementation.targetScope: Independent single-string and default-object animation over existing playback, property effects, custom effect registration and scoped DOM selectors, grouped controls, neutral keyframes/filter defaults, color/complex mixers, renderer targets and transitionEnd, renderer handoff and keyframe reads/resolution. Partial Motion implementation; not an application replacement yet.
implementation.remainingWork: Editable sequence timelines; variant propagation, arbitrary multi-axis 3D decomposition, inertia and random stagger; WAAPI, gestures/layout and full unchanged Framer Motion caller acceptance. CSS spring serialization is not implemented. Remaining runtime is unimplemented, not retained upstream code.

independentComponents.numeric interpolation: Snapshot ranges, binary lookup, custom mixers and per-segment easing
independentComponents.MotionValue: State, velocity, mutation-safe subscriptions, passive effects and owned external-animation lifecycle
independentComponents.frame scheduling: Eight ordered phases, dedupe/cancellation/keep-alive, microtasks and manual frame processing
independentComponents.numeric playback: Owned numeric keyframes, offsets and easing; millisecond generators and tween controllers with delays, repeats, seeking, speed, pause/resume and lifecycle cleanup
independentComponents.spring playback: Analytic under/critical/overdamped oscillator, velocity and retargeting; duration/visual-duration calibration; bounded settling estimates and playback integration
independentComponents.DOM effects: Deferred and coalesced style/attribute/property/SVG bindings, unit-aware transform composition, path drawing, selectors, scoped flush/release and cleanup ownership
independentComponents.numeric transition adapters: Seconds-based animateMotionValue, property defaults/overrides, owned keyframe wildcards/options and current velocity integration
independentComponents.element reads and resolution: Owner-document CSS/SVG reads, matrix extraction, bounded variable fallbacks, owned keyframes, cancellation/resume, grouped layout measurement and transactional style restoration
independentComponents.single-value animation: Numeric and string scalar/MotionValue playback with owned keyframes and options, progress mapping for colors/complex strings, finite inputs, matching-unit validation, original completion endpoints, spring overshoot, replacement safety and lifecycle error propagation.
independentComponents.element animation: animateElement and animateValues connect owned values, deferred DOM keyframe resolution, numeric controllers and shared HTML/SVG effects; public controls use seconds including delay.
independentComponents.renderer handoff: Transfers direct and pending HTML/SVG values into an existing renderer without restarting controllers; animateElement fourth argument shares renderer values and honors reduced/skip motion.
independentComponents.renderer-aware adapter: animateMotionValue returns an externally owned StartAnimation factory for numeric/CSS-unit values and custom keyframe resolvers; reused factories own snapshots, shared queues support forced resolution and restoration, skip/reduced motion and immediate handoff are honored.
independentComponents.group controls: GroupAnimation and GroupAnimationWithThen snapshot members, forward playback controls, aggregate completion, expose longest durations and dispose timeline observers; child failures do not strand remaining cleanup.
independentComponents.target completion: animateTarget resolves scalar, color and complex renderer values and per-property transitions, waits for all controllers, preserves existing end-only styles until completion, then applies owned transitionEnd snapshots in a frame; cancelled, stopped, failed (including throwing completion callbacks) or replaced targets cannot apply stale completion writes.
independentComponents.color and complex mixers: Independent hex/RGB/HSL parser, Motion gamma-two blending, balanced CSS token scanner, flat containers, automatic interpolation and renderer-owned string animation through numeric progress.
independentComponents.neutral keyframes: Property-aware neutral filter, shadow and transform values; omitted filter defaults, none/zero origins, live DOM shadow color and literal final none restoration.
independentComponents.selector animation: Fresh scoped element resolution, collection/keyframe/option snapshots, root stagger delays, grouped playback and cleanup, live owner-window reduced-motion preferences and numeric single-value forwarding.
independentComponents.custom effect registration: MotionValueState, createEffect, newest-first effect registration/removal, synchronous custom origins or optional deferred renderer resolution, scalar/color/unit animation of registered subjects and collections, grouped/scoped playback, computed rendering, explicit flush/release and subscription rollback.
independentComponents.default object animation: Unclaimed object subjects animate through existing propEffect bindings; explicit/custom effects retain priority, DOM routing stays separate, missing origins require explicit keyframes, and length fields do not turn objects into collections.
independentComponents.custom effect completion: Owned scalar transitionEnd snapshots for direct effects, registered subjects and default objects. End-only properties bind only at completion. Cancelled, failed, superseded and reentrant animations cannot apply stale ends; selectors mixing DOM and custom ends reject before playback.

changes: No upstream runtime copied; depends only on vmotion-utils.
Owns range and easing-array snapshots; rejects malformed ranges before animation starts.
Binary segment lookup bounds the cost of long numeric timelines.
Cancellation suppresses callbacks already queued in the active phase. Callback failures release processing state and allow remaining work and future frames to proceed.

Synchronous animation completion reports start before completion; late completion after cancellation does not emit a success event. Failed start hooks and throwing stop handlers release owned resources.
MotionValue retains vmotion-utils subscription lifetime protections and stops unobserved animations on the next frame, allowing same-frame resubscription.
Reversing delayed playback preserves the current value instead of reapplying a signed delay and jumping.
Paused animations release their frame callback; explicit seek, completion and cancellation apply values immediately, and callback failures clean up driver ownership.
Standalone visualDuration is honored rather than silently ignored without a bounce option.
Settled spring repeat gaps retain the endpoint; invalid retarget operations preserve the previous trajectory.
Direct element effects work across document/window boundaries; both controls silently skip a directly supplied iframe element.

Binding maps validate before attachment, stale cleanup cannot detach replacements, and queued writes are suppressed after cleanup. Nonfinite numeric styling rejects without losing other writes or future frames.
Avoids unavailable-frame wakeup setup in manual/server timing; composes transforms directly from owned binding slots without per-frame lookup arrays or unit-string helpers.

Numeric transition factories snapshot targets/options and resolve current values at start; updates and completion preserve MotionValue lifecycle ownership. Element-aware resolution is now implemented separately.

Rotated 2D scale readings retain magnitude, absent axes return identity defaults, and malformed matrices reject. Matrix decomposition uses a documented canonical convention, not recovery of the original transform function list.

DOM measurement restores owned styles and priorities before callbacks, including on failure; conflicting same-property measurements are isolated. Failed reads/callbacks do not strand unrelated queued work.
Single-value animation validates paused controllers before replacement; start/completion listener failures reject finished, while stop and cancellation settle playback and replays use fresh promises.
Resolver batches preserve any thrown value, including falsy exceptions, and restore window scroll after temporary layout measurements.

Setup owns one prepared option snapshot, creates playback promises only when observed, and caches CSS variable syntax without caching computed values. Resolver cancellation targets its read phase and allocates layout transactions only when needed.

Element animations reject unsupported targets, preserve responsive variable/percentage endpoints, share direct effect values and cancel unresolved work on release. Failed deferred resolution retains prior playback; reentrant replacement cannot reattach stale controllers.

Element controls reuse prepared numeric playback, make completion waiting lazy, and index shared render jobs once per binding. Explicit stop removes a redundant deferred unobserved-value check. Packed tests now route every test file to the installed runtime.

Element setup reuses one internal option snapshot and one lifecycle facade, avoiding duplicate controller/configuration allocations. Public factories and caller arrays remain independently snapshotted. Synchronous start-hook completion does not restart finished playback.

Renderer handoff preserves value identities, current velocity and active controllers, suppresses queued source writes and transfers pending reads. Destination validation precedes detachment, failed destination updates restore prior entries where the renderer accepts rollback, and stale source cleanup cannot detach later work.

Custom resolver output is snapshotted before conversion; constructor/prototype/instance-field errors release pending work and reject owned lifecycle promises. Resolver measurement renders between phases and restores source state, including foreign public resolver classes. isHandoff uses immediate base resolution without custom DOM reads.

Measurement guards live once per custom resolver class; source snapshots allocate only when measurement occurs. Resolved-value handoffs avoid constructing unused renderer readers. Prepared element options skip duplicate default selection while public factory snapshots and validation remain intact.

Resolver failure ownership lives in a private instance field on the cached guard class, avoiding a per-instance weak-map entry while retaining independent error routing, snapshot isolation and measurement restoration.
Grouped controls have neutral empty getters and forward every cleanup even if a child throws. Failed timeline attachment unwinds observers and returned cleanup is idempotent.

Target completion validates scalar endpoints before animation starts, owns end snapshots and suppresses stale completion after cancellation, failure, replacement or reentrant playback callbacks. Variant-state propagation is explicitly outside the implemented target contract.

Owned resolver schedulers attach failure ownership directly instead of constructing a redundant guarded subclass and scanning per-instance hooks. Foreign/custom schedulers retain guards; native read/measurement/completion failures route through the same owner and transactional restoration.

Empty frame phases return without swapping/clearing queues. Target completion uses one internal success barrier and a deferred frame write instead of materializing per-handle public lifecycle/playback promises. MotionValue completion-listener failures remain visible and suppress end writes.

CSS RGB/alpha percentages and scientific notation parse numerically; nested variables, URLs, quoted literals and identifier digits are preserved. Invalid/nonfinite colors and malformed functions reject. Flat container endpoints are snapshotted, while output containers are reused. Renderer-owned color/complex keyframes share numeric tween/spring lifecycle protections.

A single non-layout resolver bypasses batch allocation; layout reads retain isolated measurement/restoration and newly enqueued work stays out of the current transaction. Pending sets are reused and redundant cancellation of absent read callbacks is avoided.

Color and complex syntax caches are bounded to two entries each and restricted by input length; caller objects, parsed public results and mutable computed styles are never shared. Complex sampling formats components in one pass. Benchmarks include repeated and changing uncached endpoints.

Neutral filter multipliers use one (or 100%), drop shadows fade from transparent zero-length shadows and scale/matrix identities stay visible. Backdrop filters share the filter semantics. URL filters remain discrete and URL bytes are preserved. Unsupported CSS calculations/variables in neutral functions and perspective identities reject explicitly.

Empty filter arguments expand to CSS defaults, distinct from interpolation identities. Omitted shadow color is read from the owner document on each resolution. Bounded neutral-result caches retain only immutable string syntax; mutable DOM values are not cached.

Cold color parsing validates without regex match arrays or temporary channel arrays; scientific notation, percentage rules and finite checks are retained. Mixed-case none keywords keep discrete URL-filter timing.

Single pending resolvers use an inline queue slot; multi-resolver reads retain isolated transactional batches. Numeric playback cancels only its own update phase. Forced reads retain restoration and reentrant scheduling guards.

Strict common RGB parsing captures channels in one scan; hexadecimal channels use numeric extraction. The complex scanner avoids per-character substring/regex work. Prepared numeric components use fixed deltas, with a specialized two/three-length trailing-color formatter that retains finite checks and the generic parser.

Selector wrapper snapshots targets/options and resolves dynamic delays before starting. Failed element setup or scope bookkeeping stops owned controllers; cross-window HTML/SVG elements work directly. Selector animation is extended by the subsequent custom-effect and default-object/single-string units. Sequence timelines remain unfinished.

Color sampling formats rounded alpha from bounded integers; 100,001 alpha outputs, fractional channels and checked extrapolation are covered. Avoids redundant numeric resolver copies and one-use playback factories; deferred Bun setup remains slower.

Custom effects validate binding maps before invoking hooks, preserve replacement cleanup ownership and restore subscriptions after failed setup; throwing renders and teardown do not strand siblings. DOM elements retain the established renderer even when a custom predicate matches them.

Single-string playback snapshots frames, preserves raw completion endpoints and reentrant onUpdate arguments, and rejects nonfinite/unsafe input before replacement. Cross-unit conversion is unsupported without a DOM renderer; numeric strings interpolate rather than jumping. Default object origins that cannot be read reject instead of guessing. String mixer classification rejects obvious non-colors without exception allocation; candidate colors retain strict parsing.

Custom-effect completion validates before hooks, waits for every owned controller and guards binding identities and lifecycle requests. End-only writes stay deferred; failed setup restores earlier generations. The no-end path does not allocate completion bookkeeping for new subjects.

Grid stagger delays use independently calculated Euclidean/edge distances, constant-space extrema, bounded geometry caching and snapshotted dimensions; current14 comparisons cover partial rows, changed totals, fractional origins, easing and negative delays. Random ordering and editable timelines remain unimplemented.

caller.scope: Fade/transform animation and Motion value subscriptions beneath motion/react. Built foundation only; application adoption not claimed.

designReferences: Motion 14.7.0 public declarations and black-box public calls only; no upstream runtime source used.
